SfAccordion.name: SfAccordion
SfAccordion.purpose: Native details elements preserve open/close and keyboard behavior. Multiple sections may remain open.
SfAccordion.whenToUse: Use for a short list of questions or sections that readers can expand independently.
SfAccordion.avoidWhen: Do not hide required form fields or essential safety text.
SfAccordion.exampleVue:
<sf-accordion :items="[{
  title: \'Can I customize the materials?\',
  content: \'Yes. Edit the shared CSS tokens.\'
}]" />
SfAccordion.motion: Open state changes with a short transition.

items.title: How does it work?
items.content: Use native HTML controls and shared Softform tokens.

SfAdaptedCards.name: SfAdaptedCards
SfAdaptedCards.purpose: Injects a registry, normalizes the provider payload, validates an immutable CardModel array, then renders provider-agnostic notification cards.
SfAdaptedCards.whenToUse: Use when notification cards arrive from REST, GraphQL, legacy records, or a custom provider.
SfAdaptedCards.avoidWhen: Do not pass provider payloads directly to presentation cards.
SfAdaptedCards.motion: Value or highlight changes use short transitions.

notifications.subject: Design review
notifications.preview: The team left comments on the new layout.

SfAlert.name: SfAlert
SfAlert.purpose: Informational, warning, and error states. Errors use alert semantics; other messages use status.
SfAlert.whenToUse: Use for a persistent message that needs attention in the current context.
SfAlert.avoidWhen: Use SfToast for a brief confirmation that can disappear.
SfAlert.exampleVue:
<sf-alert tone="warning" title="One small thing"
  message="Review your changes before continuing." />
SfAlert.motion: Visibility and status changes use short transitions.

SfAvatar.name: SfAvatar
SfAvatar.purpose: Initials or a decorative icon, with an accessible name and three size options.
SfAvatar.whenToUse: Use an initial or icon to identify a person or source in a compact space.
SfAvatar.avoidWhen: Do not use an unlabeled avatar as the only name for a person.

SfBadge.name: SfBadge
SfBadge.purpose: Compact status, count, and metadata markers. Four treatments: default, accent, dark, outline.
SfBadge.whenToUse: Use for a short status, count, or category beside other content.
SfBadge.avoidWhen: Do not use a badge as a button or for long sentences.
SfBadge.motion: Tone and emphasis changes use short transitions.

SfBarChart.name: SfBarChart
SfBarChart.purpose: A lightweight HTML/CSS chart with a full textual data description. No canvas or chart library dependency.
SfBarChart.whenToUse: Use to compare a small sequence of values, such as activity by day.
SfBarChart.avoidWhen: Use a table when precise values matter more than the shape of the data.
SfBarChart.motion: Bars and numeric labels rise after motionDelay, with stagger between columns and motionDuration controlling the move.

SfBottomNav.name: SfBottomNav
SfBottomNav.purpose: A compact navigation bar for phone-sized layouts, with visible labels and an accent active state.
SfBottomNav.whenToUse: Use for a small set of primary destinations in a narrow layout.
SfBottomNav.avoidWhen: Do not use for a long list of routes.
SfBottomNav.motion: The selected icon fills from the previous destination; motion, delay, duration, and easing are configurable.

SfBreadcrumbs.name: SfBreadcrumbs
SfBreadcrumbs.purpose: A path with a current-page marker. Earlier items emit navigate events for your router or view state.
SfBreadcrumbs.whenToUse: Use to show a location within a hierarchy and allow movement to ancestors.
SfBreadcrumbs.avoidWhen: Do not use for steps in a linear form.
SfBreadcrumbs.motion: The active destination or panel changes with a short transition.

SfButton.name: SfButton
SfButton.purpose: Surface, dark, accent, and ghost actions. Supports icons, loading, and disabled states.
SfButton.whenToUse: Use for a discrete action such as save, create, or submit.
SfButton.avoidWhen: Use a native link for navigation.
SfButton.motion: Hover, focus, press, and disabled states respond immediately.

SfButtonGroup.name: SfButtonGroup
SfButtonGroup.purpose: A compact controlled group for related tools. It emits a new value without mutating props.
SfButtonGroup.whenToUse: Use when one compact toolbar controls a related set of choices.
SfButtonGroup.avoidWhen: Use SfRadioGroup when the choices need visible descriptions.
SfButtonGroup.motion: The pressed option fills from the previous choice; motion, delay, duration, and easing are configurable.

SfCalendar.name: SfCalendar
SfCalendar.purpose: A selectable local calendar with month navigation and arrow-key movement between dates.
SfCalendar.whenToUse: Use for choosing one date while browsing adjacent months.
SfCalendar.avoidWhen: Use a native date input when a compact form field is more useful.
SfCalendar.motion: Month grids crossfade and slide; selection changes color.

SfCheckbox.name: SfCheckbox
SfCheckbox.purpose: A native checkbox with a clear selected state, label, and disabled option.
SfCheckbox.whenToUse: Use for one independent yes or no option.
SfCheckbox.avoidWhen: Use SfRadioGroup for mutually exclusive choices.
SfCheckbox.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfClock.name: SfClock
SfClock.purpose: A real local clock. The interval is cleaned up on unmount. No server or external time service is used.
SfClock.whenToUse: Use when the user needs the current local time in a dashboard.
SfClock.avoidWhen: Do not use it as a countdown or server-time claim.
SfClock.motion: Value or highlight changes use short transitions.

SfDial.name: SfDial
SfDial.purpose: A physical dial driven by a native horizontal range. Drag left/right or use arrow keys to adjust.
SfDial.whenToUse: Use for a tactile percentage control when an approximate value is acceptable.
SfDial.avoidWhen: Use SfInput or SfStepper for a precise number.
SfDial.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfDivider.name: SfDivider
SfDivider.purpose: A hairline separator with an optional centered label.
SfDivider.whenToUse: Use to separate nearby groups or label an alternative path.
SfDivider.avoidWhen: Do not use repeated dividers to replace spacing and headings.
SfDivider.motion: Elevation and tone changes use short transitions.

SfDonutChart.name: SfDonutChart
SfDonutChart.purpose: A CSS conic-gradient ring, numeric center, and legend. Provide a percentage from 0 to 100.
SfDonutChart.whenToUse: Use to show one part of a whole with a short label.
SfDonutChart.avoidWhen: Use a table or bar chart for multiple exact comparisons.
SfDonutChart.motion: The ring and center number count toward a new percentage after motionDelay.

SfDrawer.name: SfDrawer
SfDrawer.purpose: A right-side native dialog for settings and contextual details. Its content is provided through slots.
SfDrawer.whenToUse: Use for settings or supporting details that should slide in beside the task.
SfDrawer.avoidWhen: Use SfModal for a short decision that needs centered attention.
SfDrawer.motion: The panel slides in and out with reduced-motion support.

SfDropdown.name: SfDropdown
SfDropdown.purpose: A floating action menu with outside-click dismissal, Escape, focus restoration, and arrow-key navigation.
SfDropdown.whenToUse: Use for a short list of secondary actions attached to a trigger.
SfDropdown.avoidWhen: Do not use as a form select.
SfDropdown.motion: Hover, focus, press, and disabled states respond immediately.

SfElement.name: SfElement
SfElement.purpose: Renders any native HTML tag in Vue while forwarding its attributes and slot content.
SfElement.whenToUse: Use to choose any valid native HTML root while preserving attributes and slots.
SfElement.avoidWhen: Use a specialized control when native interaction is needed.
SfElement.motion: Motion comes from the native element or its children.

SfEmptyState.name: SfEmptyState
SfEmptyState.purpose: A composed icon, title, supporting text, and optional action for a meaningful blank state.
SfEmptyState.whenToUse: Use when a collection has no items and the next action is clear.
SfEmptyState.avoidWhen: Do not show it while content is still loading.

props.name: message
props.default: 'Your collection starts with a single component.'

SfEmptyState.exampleVue:
<sf-empty-state title="All caught up."
  message="No new messages." action="New message"
  @action="compose" />
SfEmptyState.motion: Visibility and status changes use short transitions.

props.title: A little room for possibility.
props.message: Your collection starts with a single component.

SfFab.name: SfFab
SfFab.purpose: A prominent, pill-shaped entry point for a primary creation flow.
SfFab.whenToUse: Use for the main creation action when the layout can give it clear space.
SfFab.avoidWhen: Do not add several floating primary actions to one view.
SfFab.motion: Hover, focus, press, and disabled states respond immediately.

SfFileUpload.name: SfFileUpload
SfFileUpload.purpose: Choose or drop a local file. The component emits a File object; it does not send data anywhere. Accept filters the chooser only; validate dropped files in your application.
SfFileUpload.whenToUse: Use for local file selection with drag and drop feedback.
SfFileUpload.avoidWhen: Do not imply that selection uploads or stores a file.
SfFileUpload.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfIcon.name: SfIcon
SfIcon.purpose: Hand-drawn inline SVG icons. Icons are decorative; provide the accessible label on the surrounding control.
SfIcon.whenToUse: Use for a decorative symbol next to text or inside a labeled control.
SfIcon.avoidWhen: Do not use a bare icon as the only accessible action label.
SfIcon.motion: Color and scale follow the surrounding control.

SfIconButton.name: SfIconButton
SfIconButton.purpose: A tactile round control. Every instance requires a descriptive label.
SfIconButton.whenToUse: Use for a compact action whose accessible label can be concise.
SfIconButton.avoidWhen: Use SfButton when the action text should remain visible.
SfIconButton.motion: Hover, focus, press, and disabled states respond immediately.

SfInput.name: SfInput
SfInput.purpose: A native input inside an inset material, with explicit label, icon, hint, and error state.
SfInput.whenToUse: Use for a labeled single-line value with hint or error feedback.
SfInput.exampleVue:
<sf-input v-model="email" label="Email address"
  type="email" icon="mail" placeholder="you@studio.co" />
SfInput.motion: Focus, hint, error, and filled state change without moving the caret.

SfListCard.name: SfListCard
SfListCard.purpose: A compact row-based card for calls, contacts, tasks, or recent items. Emits the selected row.
SfListCard.whenToUse: Use for a short actionable list with an icon and small detail per row.
SfListCard.avoidWhen: Use SfTable for sortable multi-column records.
SfListCard.motion: Value or highlight changes use short transitions.

SfMediaPlayer.name: SfMediaPlayer
SfMediaPlayer.purpose: A working native audio element with custom controls. The demo includes an original 12-second synthesized WAV.
SfMediaPlayer.whenToUse: Use for local or supplied audio with play, mute, and seek controls.
SfMediaPlayer.avoidWhen: Do not assume that a source can autoplay.
SfMediaPlayer.motion: Playback controls respond to press and state changes.

SfMetricPanel.name: SfMetricPanel
SfMetricPanel.purpose: A dense dashboard module combining a total, two counters, and a compact activity chart.
SfMetricPanel.whenToUse: Use to combine a total, two related counts, and recent activity.
SfMetricPanel.avoidWhen: Use SfStatCard for one isolated metric.
SfMetricPanel.motion: Counters and the embedded bar chart use motionDelay, motionDuration, and stagger.

SfMixer.name: SfMixer
SfMixer.purpose: Four native vertical sliders. Changes emit a copied channel array; application audio routing is intentionally separate.
SfMixer.whenToUse: Use to adjust several related audio levels together.
SfMixer.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfModal.name: SfModal
SfModal.purpose: A native modal dialog with Escape, focus containment, focus restoration, and optional footer content.
SfModal.whenToUse: Use for a focused decision or short form that needs modal focus handling.
SfModal.avoidWhen: Do not place a long browsing flow inside a modal.
SfModal.exampleVue: Your new space starts here.
SfModal.motion: The dialog and backdrop enter and leave with reduced-motion support.

SfNavList.name: SfNavList
SfNavList.purpose: A ceramic side menu with icons, counts, and a current-page marker.
SfNavList.whenToUse: Use for a small vertical group of destinations or sections.
SfNavList.avoidWhen: Do not use for arbitrary action buttons.
SfNavList.motion: The selected row fills from the previous destination; motion, delay, duration, and easing are configurable.

SfNotification.name: SfNotification
SfNotification.purpose: A small content card with stable presentation props. It knows nothing about REST, GraphQL, or legacy payloads.
SfNotification.whenToUse: Use to show one message, call, or status update with sender and action.
SfNotification.avoidWhen: Use SfAdaptedCards to normalize a collection from a provider.

props.name: body
props.default: 'Your new component library is ready to explore.'

SfNotification.exampleVue:
<sf-notification title="Design review" sender="Maya Chen"
  body="The new surfaces are ready." time="09:41"
  :count="4" icon="mail" @action="openMessage" />
SfNotification.motion: Value or highlight changes use short transitions.

props.title: Design review
props.body: Your new component library is ready to explore.

SfPagination.name: SfPagination
SfPagination.purpose: A controlled page selector with bounded previous and next actions.
SfPagination.whenToUse: Use to move through known pages of a collection.
SfPagination.avoidWhen: Do not use when total pages are unknown.
SfPagination.motion: The current page fills from the previous page; motion, delay, duration, and easing are configurable.

SfProfileCard.name: SfProfileCard
SfProfileCard.purpose: A reusable profile composition with initials, status, role, and an action affordance.
SfProfileCard.whenToUse: Use to summarize one person, role, and availability.
SfProfileCard.avoidWhen: Do not use for a full editable profile form.

SfProgress.name: SfProgress
SfProgress.purpose: A native progress element with a label and numeric output. Values represent real state supplied by the host.
SfProgress.whenToUse: Use when task completion can be expressed as a percentage.
SfProgress.avoidWhen: Use SfSpinner when progress cannot be measured.
SfProgress.motion: The native progress value and label count toward the supplied percentage after motionDelay.

SfRadioGroup.name: SfRadioGroup
SfRadioGroup.purpose: Mutually exclusive native inputs with fieldset and legend semantics.
SfRadioGroup.whenToUse: Use for one choice among a labeled set of options.
SfRadioGroup.avoidWhen: Use SfSelect if the list is long and space is limited.
SfRadioGroup.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfRating.name: SfRating
SfRating.purpose: Keyboard-operable star selection with radio semantics. Arrow keys, Home, and End are supported.
SfRating.whenToUse: Use for a small ordered rating that supports keyboard selection.
SfRating.avoidWhen: Do not use for a precise numeric measurement.
SfRating.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfSegmented.name: SfSegmented
SfSegmented.purpose: A native radio group in an inset tray. Use for view modes or mutually exclusive settings.
SfSegmented.whenToUse: Use for a few short view or filter modes with one active choice.
SfSegmented.avoidWhen: Use SfTabs when each choice owns a content panel.
SfSegmented.motion: The checked segment fills from the previous option; motion, delay, duration, and easing are configurable.

SfSelect.name: SfSelect
SfSelect.purpose: A native select preserves operating-system pickers and keyboard behavior.
SfSelect.whenToUse: Use a native picker for a compact list of options.
SfSelect.avoidWhen: Use SfRadioGroup when every option should stay visible.
SfSelect.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfSkeleton.name: SfSkeleton
SfSkeleton.purpose: A loading placeholder, with reduced-motion support and a status label.
SfSkeleton.whenToUse: Use to reserve the shape of content during a pending load.
SfSkeleton.avoidWhen: Do not use it after an empty response is known.
SfSkeleton.motion: A low-contrast shimmer indicates pending content.

SfSlider.name: SfSlider
SfSlider.purpose: A native range input with output, limits, units, and optional end labels.
SfSlider.whenToUse: Use for an adjustable bounded number with a visible value.
SfSlider.avoidWhen: Use SfStepper or SfInput when exact entry is central.
SfSlider.motion: The track and value respond while dragging.

SfSpinner.name: SfSpinner
SfSpinner.purpose: Small, regular, and large loading indicators. The status label can be customized.
SfSpinner.whenToUse: Use for an indeterminate wait inside or near an action.
SfSpinner.avoidWhen: Use SfProgress when completion can be measured.
SfSpinner.motion: A small rotation indicates indeterminate progress.

SfStatCard.name: SfStatCard
SfStatCard.purpose: A large figure, label, icon, change marker, and supporting context.
SfStatCard.whenToUse: Use for one important metric with context and a short change label.
SfStatCard.avoidWhen: Use SfMetricPanel when two counts and a trend belong together.
SfStatCard.exampleVue:
<sf-stat-card label="Messages" :value="128"
  change="+12.8%" description="since last week" icon="mail" />
SfStatCard.motion: Numeric values count toward the supplied value after motionDelay; strings use a short text transition.

SfStepper.name: SfStepper
SfStepper.purpose: Increment, decrement, or type a numeric value. Every change is clamped to the provided limits.
SfStepper.whenToUse: Use to adjust a small integer quantity within known limits.
SfStepper.avoidWhen: Use SfSlider for a broad approximate range.
SfStepper.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfSurface.name: SfSurface
SfSurface.purpose: The shared ceramic material. Use the default raised treatment, a low elevation, a flat card, or an inset well.
SfSurface.whenToUse: Use as a card, section, article, or inset well with Softform material.
SfSurface.avoidWhen: Do not use it to replace a meaningful document heading.
SfSurface.motion: Elevation and tone changes use short transitions.

SfSwitch.name: SfSwitch
SfSwitch.purpose: A native checkbox exposed as a switch. The tiny yellow thumb indicates the on state.
SfSwitch.whenToUse: Use for an immediate on or off setting.
SfSwitch.avoidWhen: Use SfCheckbox when the option is part of a later form submission.
SfSwitch.motion: Selection and focus states use short transitions.

SfTable.name: SfTable
SfTable.purpose: A semantic table with sortable column headers. Data is copied before sorting, never mutated in place.
SfTable.whenToUse: Use for multi-column records that need sorting and a caption.
SfTable.avoidWhen: Use SfListCard for a short single-line list.
SfTable.motion: Search, sorting, paging, and table or card views respond to the supplied rows.

SfTabs.name: SfTabs
SfTabs.purpose: A controlled tablist with roving focus, linked tab panel, and directional keyboard navigation.
SfTabs.whenToUse: Use when one of several labeled panels is visible at a time.
SfTabs.avoidWhen: Use SfSegmented for a short filter that does not own a panel.
SfTabs.motion: The active tab and panel change with a short transition.

SfTextarea.name: SfTextarea
SfTextarea.purpose: A controlled native textarea with a live character count and maximum length.
SfTextarea.whenToUse: Use for multi-line writing with a character limit.
SfTextarea.motion: Focus and character-count feedback change while typing.

props.modelValue: A clear note for the team.
props.label: Notes

SfTimeline.name: SfTimeline
SfTimeline.purpose: An ordered activity list with connectors, descriptions, and times.
SfTimeline.whenToUse: Use for events whose order and time are meaningful.
SfTimeline.avoidWhen: Use SfListCard when the entries are actions without chronology.
SfTimeline.motion: Value or highlight changes use short transitions.

SfToast.name: SfToast
SfToast.purpose: A compact live status message with an optional dismiss action. Placement and timing belong to the host app.
SfToast.whenToUse: Use for brief confirmation of a completed local action.
SfToast.avoidWhen: Use SfAlert for persistent errors or guidance.
SfToast.motion: Visibility and status changes use short transitions.

SfTooltip.name: SfTooltip
SfTooltip.purpose: A hint shown on hover or focus. The slot receives its tooltip id to attach with aria-describedby.
SfTooltip.whenToUse: Use to explain a compact control on hover or focus.
SfTooltip.avoidWhen: Do not hide essential instructions in a tooltip.
SfTooltip.exampleVue:
<sf-tooltip text="Saved to your collection" v-slot="{ describedby }">
  <sf-icon-button icon="heart" label="Save item"
    :aria-describedby="describedby" />
</sf-tooltip>
SfTooltip.motion: Visibility and status changes use short transitions.

SfWorkflow.name: SfWorkflow
SfWorkflow.purpose: A set of physical-looking nodes joined by hairlines. Selection is controlled by the parent.
SfWorkflow.whenToUse: Use to show a short sequence of connected stages and the active stage.
SfWorkflow.avoidWhen: Do not use it for a large editable flowchart.
SfWorkflow.motion: Value or highlight changes use short transitions.
